brief: Dādī telling the legend with a hand raised; behind her, a faint painted vision of a sage by a river looking up at a hunter who has lowered his bow, and a pair of cranes, one fallen, one crying; Chandikā listening with her drum in her lap; Śuka perched wide-eyed on the throne; Lubdhaka at the back, no longer smiling.

Behind a slid-open stone panel, a tall thin spirit of pale smoke drifting in a ring around the golden throne, her long sleeves trailing, one hand counting on her fingers; Dādī and Śuka watching from the opening; Chandikā's small drum resting on the throne's arm; warm light.

The thirty-second statue, the last, stern-faced, with a very small hand held up showing two fingers; at her feet the throne itself, bare and plain; Dādī and Śuka looking up at her; Lubdhaka's foreman at the back, quiet.
The thirty-first statue holding a small stone bowl in which a golden sun rises; carved lotuses opening along her plinth; Dādī pointing at the sun; Śuka watching; early gold light in the hall.
The twenty-fourth statue holding a small purse of coins that clink; Dādī counting a few on her palm; Śuka trying words aloud; Lubdhaka's foreman eyeing the purse hungrily.

The twenty-fifth statue holding a pair of stone scales that tilt gently; Dādī pointing at the beam; Śuka perched on one pan which sinks slightly; Lubdhaka's foreman watching the scales hold his breath.
The twenty-third statue holding a shallow bowl of still water that shivers; Dādī touching the rim; Śuka looking into the water at three faces reflected: a man, a god, a stone; lamplight on the water.

The seventh statue with a finger lifted to her lips, a fine mist of breath leaving her mouth and drifting up in the cold air; Śuka testing words with a raised wing; Dādī listening; Lubdhaka's foreman at a distance holding a lamp.
